spots.desc: Also known a Chop Alley a multitude of little stalls offer everything from functional modern rubber stamps to hand carved traditional Chinese seals, you can pick out a stone seal and have it personalised with your name, your name in Chinese (many stores will have on display a list of popular transliterations of Western names into Chinese characters) your initials, or even your own design. The…

spots.name: Dumpling House
spots.desc: Great Beijing-style dumplings, avoid going there during lunch hour, because it is packed.

spots.name: Good Luck Thai
spots.desc: Seating is both indoors and outdoors, very popular on weekends, nice atmosphere.

spots.name: Wai Kee Congee Shop
spots.desc: A good place to sample some traditional Hong Kong style food.

spots.name: XTC Gelato
spots.desc: A popular place to get your fix of ice cream or frozen yoghurt.

spots.name: L16 Cafe and Bar
spots.desc: Serves Thai and Italian food, but come for the location - not the food. A rare place to drink and eat outside away from the noise of Central.
spots.addr: Hong Kong Park, 19 Cotton Tree Drive

spots.name: Maxim's Palace
spots.desc: One of Hong Kong's most popular dim sum spots, featuring harbour views if you're lucky enough to score a window table. The atmosphere and food are very much in the classical dim sum tradition, a large, noisy hall with waitresses pushing around carts laden with goodies; try the siu mai (燒賣), har gao (蝦餃) and mango pudding. Dim sum served 11AM-3PM daily, expect to queue on Sundays (when the…

spots.name: Yung Kee Restaurant
spots.desc: This is a popular place for Cantonese-style roast goose and century eggs. Come early and make reservations as they have been known to run out of geese!

spots.name: Beirut
spots.desc: Lebanese cuisine is top of the sheet. Lamb or chicken kebab and sisha. Nice decor but the food is a far cry from the real deal (particularly in taste).

spots.name: Fung Shing Restaurant
spots.desc: Very local eatery known for its dim sum, which is cheap and good at $10 and up per serving. Open daily from 7:30AM for the dim sum breakfast crowd, but no English menu.

spots.name: Al Dente
spots.desc: Italian cuisine. Serving large, medium quality dishes not too different from what you would find in an Italian bistro. Their pastas and meat dishes are better than their pizzas. Often full.
spots.addr: 16 Staunton St, Soho (中環蘇豪士丹頓街16號地下)

spots.name: Ayuthaiya
spots.desc: Thai cuisine. Serving quite authentic food in a stylish, dark environment.
spots.addr: 35 Hollywood Rd, Soho (中環荷李活道35號)

spots.name: Brunch Club
spots.desc: Neighbourhood-style Western coffee shop (pre-Starbucks style) specialising in brunch and breakfast, although dinner is also served. Customers are provided with a wide range of newspapers and magazines in English and Chinese. Clientele is mainly expatriate.

spots.name: Double Happiness Cafe
spots.desc: Shanghai cuisine. Nice and simple little restaurant serving authentic Shanghainese dishes. Prices reflects that this is in the centre of Soho and comparable food can be found much cheaper elsewhere.

spots.name: Jashan
spots.desc: Indian cuisine. Serves great curries and perfect naan. The lunch buffet is good value.

spots.name: Oola
spots.desc: Away from the crowds in Soho, but worth the extra walk. International menu in a comfortable environment. Serves as both a place to eat or drink. Drinks are expensive.
spots.addr: G/F, Centre Stage, Bridges St, Soho

spots.name: The Peak Lookout
spots.desc: Serving a range of international cuisine such as naan bread, Hainan chicken, and steaks in a 19th-century heritage building. Also has a pleasant garden patio.

spots.name: 8½ Otto e Mezzo Bombana
spots.desc: Only Italian restaurant outside Italy to be awarded three Michelin stars.

spots.name: Chez Patrick
spots.desc: An excellent, Parisian-style French restaurant. The proprietor, Patrick, has a delightful obsession with foie gras which extends to creative dishes such as foie gras ice cream served as a first course.

spots.name: Chilli Fagara
spots.desc: Sichuan cuisine. Great spicy dishes including the favourites you will find in Sichuan Province. This restaurant's ambitions appear to go further than just making the food as the mainland original implying that some might be disappointed. Somewhat overpriced but still good.

spots.name: Luk Yu Tea House
spots.desc: Famous for the excellent tea and traditional dim sum. It is a popular meeting place for businessmen. They provide an English menu on request.

spots.name: Works
spots.desc: A good place for tourists to start on the gay bar-scene. Popular with expats and tourists alike, it is easily accessible in Central. Friday and Saturday are the most popular nights but do not expect many drinkers to arrive much before 11PM.

spots.name: 65 Peel
spots.desc: A bar with a very Hong Kong aesthetic serving cocktails and a range of locally brewed beer.

spots.name: The Globe
spots.desc: Excellent beer pub, also has good menu aimed at western taste buds. It is also one of the few places that has Typhoon T8 on tap, a locally produced cask ale.

spots.name: Staunton's Wine Bar & Cafe
spots.desc: A western-style restaurant with a bar on the ground floor and table service upstairs.

spots.name: Windsurfing memorial statute
spots.desc: On Cheung Chau, visitors should also look out for this statue which commemorates a Hong Kong windsurfing athlete, Lee Lai-shan (李麗珊), who won the first Olympic gold medal for the territory.

spots.name: Tai Shek Hau Tin Hau Temple
spots.desc: Tin Hau, the queen of heaven is the god who receives the most respect from many who live on Cheung Chau, especially those who are fishermen. Tin Hau is revered as the god who protects fisherman. Tin Hau has been respected for many years, and so there are four Tin Hau Temples on the island.

spots.name: Kwun Yam Temple
spots.desc: A smaller bright red temple building dating back before 1840, dedicated to the 'Goddess of Mercy'.

spots.name: Sai Wan Tin Hau Temple
spots.desc: A smaller temple dedicated to the Goddess Tin Hau, who is associated with the sea and fishermen. The temple commands good views out to sea.

spots.name: Birthday of Tin Hau
spots.desc: Besides the Bun Festival, another big festival is the birthday of Tin Hau. Tin Hau is the "queen of the heaven" and is closely associated with seafarers and fishermen. The birthday of Tin Hau is in the Chinese calendar on the 23rd day of the third lunar month. However, people in Cheung Chau usually celebrate it on the 18th, because in the past, there were no street lights on the island and people…

spots.name: Cheung Chau Market
spots.desc: The Cheung Chau market is similar to other 'wet markets' in Hong Kong, offering a wide variety of fresh produce.
spots.addr: Cheung Chau Municipal Services Building, 2 Tai Hing Tai Rd

spots.name: Cheung Chau Cooked Food Market
spots.desc: A covered, open-air set of connected restaurants selling a number of different varieties of Chinese food and seafood.

spots.name: Dr Sun Yat-sen Museum
spots.desc: Exhibits on the life of Sun Yat-sen.

spots.name: Sheung Wan Civic Centre
spots.desc: Theatre and concert venue.
spots.addr: 5/F., Sheung Wan Municipal Services Building, 345 Queen's Road Central,

spots.name: Yan Shang Kee
spots.desc: Rent a qipao to wear for a day while exploring Hong Kong.

spots.name: Hollywood Road
spots.desc: Antiques.

spots.name: Law Fu Kee
spots.desc: Popular little restaurant serving congee and noodles.

spots.name: Zhong Guo Song
spots.desc: Good Chinese food, without MSG and less oil.
spots.addr: Wo On Lane, Lan Kwai Fong

spots.name: Pizza Express
spots.desc: Has a nice view overlooking the Mid-Levels Escalator.

spots.name: Baci
spots.desc: Pizza.

spots.name: Tokyo Joe
spots.desc: Japanese food.

spots.name: La Pampa
spots.desc: Argentinian.

spots.name: Percy Bakery
spots.desc: A high quality bakery. Take away and delivery service only.
spots.addr: Shop b, g/f, 68 Catchick St, Kennedy Town

spots.name: Bistro Bouchon
spots.desc: French bistro focusing on steaks.

spots.name: HAHAClub
spots.desc: For cheaper booze, you can try here.

spots.name: de België
spots.desc: A bar specialising in Belgian beers.

spots.name: Craft Brew & Co
spots.desc: A corner bar with a selection of craft beer on tap.

spots.name: Propaganda
spots.desc: Famous gay club. Tends to get going after Works has faded.

spots.name: Nam Tam Wan Tin Hau Temple
Windsurfing & Sunbathing
spots.desc: The prime drawcards on the beaches of Cheung Chau.

spots.name: Yin Hop Company
spots.desc: A small bicycle rental shop and bicycle mechanic along the main market street.

spots.name: 宜佳公司
spots.desc: A larger bike shop that is slightly further away from the ferry pier. This shop also has tricycles and quadracycles for rent.

spots.name: Peng Chau Leather Factory
spots.desc: An outdoor consisting of a garden and a painted underpass that hosts a constantly-changing art exhibition by local artists. The site is built around the remains of a ruined old leather factory (hence the name).

spots.name: Tin Hau Temple
spots.desc: The Tin Hau temple dates back to 1792 which houses a whale rib. Outside the Tin Hau Temple there is a stone monument warning about pirates.

spots.name: Lung Mo Temple
spots.desc: One of the larger temples on the island that opens onto a beach.

spots.name: Finger Hill
spots.desc: Head for Finger Hill which is popular for the panoramic views of the island, Disneyland and the Tsing Ma Bridge.

spots.name: Ngan Chau Pavillion
spots.desc: A covered pavillion among an NGO-run ecological project. The area is very open and affords good photo opportunities of the islands to the East of the island, looking back towards Hong Kong Island. The area is easily reachable by walking down the other side of Finger Hill.

spots.name: Tung Wan Beach
spots.desc: Don't miss the beach at Tung Wan, from there you can head north through the small farms until you reach the north shore of the island, that still retains 60% of its natural seashore. Around the coast there is a diversity of marine life, including Chinese white dolphins, and some of Hong Kong's few remaining coral reefs.

spots.name: Old Fisherman's Rock
spots.desc: An interesting rock formation sitting atop a small sandy island slightly off the north-east coast of the island. It is reachable across a slightly submerged sandbar.

spots.name: Tai Lei Island
spots.desc: A smaller island off the coast of Peng Chau which houses some support facilities such as a waste handling facility. The bridge to the island is a popular fishing spot for locals.

spots.name: Come Be Rich Restaurant
spots.desc: A popular local banquet restaurant close to the ferry pier. This establishment has outdoor seating and is popular with families and large groups. The conversations here can get quite loud towards closing time.

spots.name: Fooderful
spots.desc: A larger restaurant with entrances at both ends and outdoor seating out the back facing towards the ferry pier. Most of the dishes are larger and intended to be shared, so this is more suitable for those coming in groups.

spots.name: Hoi King Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: A local seafood restaurant that also does traditional Hong Kong-style Yumcha dishes.

spots.name: Kee Sum Cafe
spots.desc: A very popular restaurant at the end of Wing On Street which is a very popular breakfast spot with locals.
spots.addr: Shop B, G/F, 3 Peng Chau Wing On Street

spots.name: Peng Chau Si Do
spots.desc: A shop selling cold drinks and local Hong Kong snacks situated within the main ferry pier.

spots.name: Wah Kee Snacks
spots.desc: A local-style snack shop up one of the smaller alleys off the main shopping street.

spots.name: Tino Club Thai Food
spots.desc: A Thai restaurant on the Nam Wan Road with outdoor and indoor seating.

spots.name: Viet Restaurant
spots.desc: A Vietnamese restaurant on the main shopping street less than 5 minutes walk from the ferry pier.

spots.name: Paris Cafe
spots.desc: A newer establishment that sells local takes on more Westernised food.

spots.name: The Old China Hand
spots.desc: This is the one and only pub on Peng Chau. It serves draft beers and caters for the needs of most drinkers. Staff speak English, Cantonese, Japanese and Mandarin.

spots.name: SunSatStore
spots.desc: A small cafe / store selling a variety of antiques, crafts, and other objects that the owners have collected through their travels around the world.
